title: The comparison pullback is exact on sheaves of modules and commutes with cohomology sheaves
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite discrete commutative ring. Let $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the small pro-etale site of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}$ and $\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$ be the constant sheaves of rings with value $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on them, and let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism of sites, with inverse image $
u_T^{-1}$ on sheaves [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Then:

1. $
u_T^{-1}\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}\cong\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$ as sheaves of rings, so $
u_T$ is a flat morphism of ringed sites $(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}})	o(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{et}}})$ and the module inverse image $
u_T^*F=
u_T^{-1}F\otimes_{
u_T^{-1}\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}}\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$ of a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ is $
u_T^{-1}F$ with its induced $\Lambda$-module structure.
2. The functor $
u_T^*:\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)	o\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ between the abelian categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is additive and exact (it preserves finite limits and finite colimits).
3. Consequently, for every cochain complex $K$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and every $i\in\mathbf Z$ there is an isomorphism $\mathcal H^i(
u_T^*K)\cong
u_T^*\mathcal H^i(K)$, natural in $K$, between the cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] of the termwise pullback and the pullback of the cohomology sheaves. In particular termwise $
u_T^*$ carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, and carries a complex whose cohomology sheaves vanish in degrees $<a$ to a complex whose cohomology sheaves vanish in degrees $<a$.

proof.text: Work in the larger universe in which the chosen site representatives are small. Write $L=\nu_T^{-1}$ and $R=\nu_{T,*}$. The comparison-morphism node gives $L\dashv R$, with $L$ preserving finite limits and $R$ given by restriction along the inclusion of sites. In particular the terminal object $T/T$ is sent to $T/T$, so $(RG)(T)=G(T)$. Apply the finite-product adjunction lifting theorem to obtain the adjunction on commutative ring objects. Under the equivalence between ring objects of the sheaf topos and ring sheaves, this is an adjunction $L_{\mathrm{ring}}\dashv R_{\mathrm{ring}}$ on ring sheaves, with underlying set functor $L$. This use is a generic algebraic-structure tool, not an assertion of module exactness.

proof.text:
Put $A=\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}$ and $B=\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$. For every pro-etale sheaf of commutative rings $G$, the ring adjunction and the constant-sheaf universal property give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(L_{\mathrm{ring}}A,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,R_{\mathrm{ring}}G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{CRing}}(\Lambda,G(T))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,G).$$
Denote this natural bijection by $\Phi_G$, put $X=L_{\mathrm{ring}}A$, and set $c=\Phi_B^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_B):X\to B$ and $d=\Phi_X(\mathrm{id}_X):B\to X$. Naturality gives $\Phi_X(dc)=d\Phi_B(c)=d=\Phi_X(\mathrm{id}_X)$ and $cd=c\Phi_X(\mathrm{id}_X)=\Phi_B(c)=\mathrm{id}_B$; injectivity of $\Phi_X$ gives $dc=\mathrm{id}_X$. Hence $c:L_{\mathrm{ring}}A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ is a ring-sheaf isomorphism. More explicitly its adjoint $A\to R_{\mathrm{ring}}B$ is the map extending $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\in B(T)$, so this is the canonical constant-coefficient comparison, with its ring structure and all constant sections fixed. The only calculation here is composition of the cited natural bijections.

For an $A$-module sheaf $F$, apply $L$ to its addition, zero, negation and action $A\times F\to F$. The finite-product comparisons identify the latter map with $L_{\mathrm{ring}}A\times LF\to LF$; applying $L$ to each module-axiom diagram proves the module axioms, and applying $L$ to the action-compatibility square proves functoriality. This is the induced module structure of the comparison-morphism node, expressed as a variable-ring action. Give $LF$ the $B$-action $b\cdot m=c^{-1}(b)m$, using $c$ from step 2. To check agreement with the fixed-$\Lambda$ construction, let $a_\lambda:*\to A$ and $b_\lambda:*\to B$ be the constant sections associated to $\lambda\in\Lambda$. The description of the adjunct of $c$ in step 2 and naturality of the adjunction unit give $c\circ L(a_\lambda)=b_\lambda$, using $L(*)\cong *$. Therefore multiplication by $b_\lambda$ on $LF$ is $L$ of multiplication by $a_\lambda$ on $F$, exactly the scalar endomorphism specified in the comparison-morphism node. The module adjunction theorem identifies ringed-site pullback with $LF\otimes_{L_{\mathrm{ring}}A}B$, whose canonical map to the transported $LF$ is $m\otimes b\mapsto c^{-1}(b)m$ and whose inverse is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. The tensor relation makes these maps inverse on each sectionwise tensor product; they commute with restrictions and hence on the associated sheaves. For any module sheaf over $L_{\mathrm{ring}}A$ these formulas identify extension of scalars along $c$ with the same underlying abelian sheaf endowed with the displayed $B$-action, with inverse restriction along $c$. Kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels retain their underlying abelian sheaves by the module-category node, so this extension of scalars is exact. Equivalently $B$ is flat over $L_{\mathrm{ring}}A$, which is precisely flatness of this morphism of ringed sites. This proves clause 1.

proof.text: Apply the abelian inverse-image exactness theorem to the comparison morphism. Its hypotheses are satisfied by step 1: this is a morphism of sites inducing a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint. Hence $L_{\mathrm{Ab}}$ is additive and preserves kernels and cokernels of abelian sheaves. After forgetting module actions, the functor of step 3 is exactly $L_{\mathrm{Ab}}$: both act by $L$ on the underlying sheaf and on its group operations. Kernels of module maps are the sectionwise kernels with restricted scalar action; cokernels are the sheafifications of sectionwise quotients with the descended scalar action, as specified by the module-category node. These are also the underlying abelian kernels and cokernels, because the same inclusions and quotient maps have those universal properties after forgetting scalars. Therefore the kernel and cokernel comparisons for $\nu_T^*$ are isomorphisms: they are module maps and are isomorphisms on underlying abelian sheaves; the inverse of a bijective module homomorphism is linear. Additivity follows from $L_{\mathrm{Ab}}$ and faithfulness of forgetting. An additive functor preserves zero and finite biproducts: apply it to the identities for biproduct injections and projections. For a finite diagram $D:J\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, its limit is the kernel of the map $\bigoplus_{j\in\mathrm{Ob}(J)}D(j)\to\bigoplus_{(a:j\to k)\in\mathrm{Mor}(J)}D(k)$ with $a$-component $D(a)x_j-x_k$: factoring through this kernel says exactly that the components form a cone. Its colimit is the cokernel of $\bigoplus_{(a:j\to k)\in\mathrm{Mor}(J)}D(j)\to\bigoplus_{j\in\mathrm{Ob}(J)}D(j)$, sending an element $y$ in the $a$-summand to $D(a)y$ in the $k$-summand minus $y$ in the $j$-summand: killing these relations says exactly that a map is a cocone. These formulas include the empty diagram, with empty biproduct equal to zero. Thus $\nu_T^*$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits, proving clause 2.

proof.text:
The two module-sheaf categories are abelian by the module-category node, and step 4 makes $
u_T^*$ an exact additive functor between them. Apply the exact-functor complex-cohomology theorem in every integer degree. It gives
$$c_K^i:\mathcal H^i(
u_T^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_T^*\mathcal H^i(K),$$
natural in $K$, with the indicated direction. In concrete terms the theorem identifies the kernel of the pulled-back differential with the pulled-back cycle sheaf and the image of the preceding differential with the pulled-back boundary sheaf, then identifies their quotient. Thus these are the cohomology sheaves defined in the cohomology-sheaf node, not cohomology of the presheaves of sections. The theorem applies to arbitrary cochain complexes, with no boundedness assumption.

proof.text:
For a quasi-isomorphism $h:K	o K'$, naturality of the isomorphisms in step 5 gives $c_{K'}^i\mathcal H^i(
u_T^*h)=
u_T^*(\mathcal H^i(h))c_K^i$. The right-hand cohomology map is an isomorphism because every functor preserves inverse pairs. Consequently the pulled-back map is a quasi-isomorphism. If $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i<a$, step 5 and $
u_T^*0=0$ give $\mathcal H^i(
u_T^*K)=0$ for every $i<a$. This proves both final assertions of clause 3, including arbitrary negative degrees.
